title: Where a guarded command runs
text: Write guards and the workspace-cwd writer guard resolve a relative path in the directory of the segment it appears in: the command's declared workdir, moved by every plain `cd` before that segment, including a `cd` after an earlier command. A `cd $NAME` resolves through an assignment written before it (a literal path or an `mktemp` result) and bare assignment statements do not end the leading-`cd` walk; an assignment written after the `cd`, an unbound or opaque variable, a backtick or `cd -` leaves later directories unknown, so the declared workdir still applies. A `git commit` without `-C` reads the repository its segment moved to with a literal `cd`. Codex carries the workdir only in its local rollout; the hook client stamps it, matching a code-mode call by its exact command when the hook id is the inner item id, and resolves a `workdir` written as a bare identifier only from a single literal `const`/`let`/`var` binding with no reassignment. The client's own path answer is used only when it names the same path, so a client that missed the directory cannot move a lane write onto main. Observed in source and tests; deployed harness proof is pending. Direct exec_command rollout arguments and the input payload container carry the same workdir authority. Python temporary-directory/file factories and computed scratch prefixes avoid a false cwd target; explicit source writes and unresolved non-scratch writes retain checks. Registered checkout and lane boundaries take precedence over scratch-root inference, including checkouts stored in temporary directories. Literal list or tuple loops whose every path is scratch also avoid cwd fallback; mixed or unknown loop destinations remain unresolved and checked. The session-cwd claim check applies only inside recorded repository roots and their lanes; external paths need no claim. Installed harness and Yoke release paths, including uv release trees, remain read-only. The main-write guard protects the main checkout, and lane occupancy still refuses foreign writes. Shared path resolution removes glued shell separators and unmatched closing parentheses from operands, including path flags and subshell endings, while retaining quoted or escaped filename punctuation and punctuation in bound variables.
